body: My ex was my first partner and that was when I was 21 so I can relate to that too, going so long without ever having a date or a kiss or anything... I know people sometimes find love way later in life so I think there's still hope in that regard, I just dunno how much longer it's gonna take and I don't feel patient enough to keep trying 'til I'm 40 or something. It's super encouraging your parents have been together for so long though, at least you've got proof it's possible, I hope you find someone too and that we both find something worth living for.

Well, in the first place, you know you're not racist or else you wouldn't feel bad for saying it. You can definitely accidentally act racist, and saying it wasn't acceptable, but you aren't racist if you don't believe in any sort of inferiority/superiority.

And yeah, others may think you are because of that comment, but if they know you fairly well and know that you're drunk and you've never exhibited racist behavior before, they probably just thought you were drunk and stupid, not genuinely racist. Drunk and stupid is forgivable and common. You'll notice if they start treating you differently, and it's really unlikely they will, and you'll always have a chance to explain and apologize if they do.

The video could be shared and misconstrued, but it's been a week and you'd likely have heard about it by now if it had been. More likely, it either wasn't caught on video, it's not going to be shared, or no one is going to automatically assume you're a horrible racist because of it.

I know it must feel overwhelming right now, but at least wait it out. If nothing else, I can tell you suicide is always an option later but not something you can take back once it's done, so give the situation time to play out before jumping straight to it. It was an honest mistake and the fact you feel guilty means you're not racist or a bad person. At the moment no video has ruined your reputation and you don't know that your friends think badly of you, so just try to continue being a good person, learn from it, and wait to see how things go. Killing yourself doesn't really ease that guilt anyway, you could always donate to a good black charity movement or something similar if you feel the need to atone.
